body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 7430effad9686137e23483439a8b1e928017a4e1 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers found. Because this is a `feat`, it merges at the next cut.

This was a high-tier review: a new toolpath generator falls under the safety floor, so most of the effort went into gouge and crash safety.

### What looks good
- **The loops stay inside the channel.** Every front arc meets the band walls at |v| = B ≤ room, and the fillet stays inside the band. The bore has radius B, and the far end is closed by the cap arcs. `contained()` (`trochoid_slot.rs:244`) checks each arc at 1° spacing against the cutter-centre band and refuses by name. The leads between loops run along the wall, and on the straight `a -> b` line the op passes they lie on the band edge.
- **Returns are safe by construction, and checked as well.** The microlift retraces the arc it just cut, and a retract comes back down to the same piece's start, so both land where the tool already cut at that level. `lifted_cut` reads the inside of the cutter disc against the in-process dexel stock, and the planner refuses if any lifted move would stand over stock.
- **Engagement is measured, not assumed.** Each candidate step is measured on the dexel stock down the step ladder; if no step holds the limit, the op is refused with the lowest reading, where it was read, and at which step. On a straight line, loop and cap counts are capped (`MAX_LOOPS`, the clamps in `arc_samples` and in `lifted_cut`'s sampler), so nothing loops without bound.
- **No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.** `Chain::new` guarantees at least two points, so the indexing in `Chain::at` and `Chain::dir` is safe, and every `as usize` cast takes a finite, clamped value.
- **The kind id is consistent.** Kind id and tag 40 agree across `KindInfo` (tag 40, ordinal 40), `ribbon.rs`, `probe_op.rs` and the `stamp_follows_every_input` count of 41. The project file uses its own `trochoidal_slot` params arm (`trochoid_dto.rs`), so it stores no numeric id. Tip commit 7430effa only changes `crates/app/src/operation/tests.rs`: the count goes from 40 to 41 plus a comment.
- **`sane.rs` validates at command creation.** It refuses non-finite endpoints, width, step, engagement outside (0, 180], a microlift height of zero or less, negative smoothing or stock to leave, insane heights, and non-positive stepdown or feeds.
- **MCP is covered by the generic tools.** `create_operation` and `edit_operation` resolve kinds through `KindInfo::ALL` and patch params through the params DTO, so the new kind is reachable with no tool of its own.
- **The UI page follows Everything Is a Command.** `trochoid_page.rs` only edits the page draft, and Apply goes through `EditOperationParams`; `trochoid_op.rs` pins create/edit undo and redo.
- New modules carry provenance lines and the new files stay under 400 lines. The PR touches no `build.rs`, `.github/`, scripts, dependencies or process files, and no snapshot PNGs.

### Local results (worktree at head 7430effa; `upstream/main` merges in with no conflicts - "Already up to date")
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| motion `trochoid_slot` | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| app `trochoid_op` | 4 passed, 0 failed |
| app `golden_cl trochoid` (`trochoid_slot_small_matches_golden`) | 1 passed; golden unchanged |
| app `fanuc_post` (includes `trochoid_slot_small.nc`) | 11 passed |
| app `ribbon` (trochoid), `probe_op` (appends), lib `stamp_follows_every_input` | 1 + 1 + 1 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Adversarial checks (a local scratch test, not committed).**
- **Containment sweep, 1152 cases.** Tool D 3/6/10; width 1.1/1.6/3 x D; step 0.05/0.3/1/2.5 x D; smoothing 0/2; climb and conventional; microlift and retract; lines that are horizontal, diagonal, 4 mm and 0.3 mm long.
  - 968 plans came back and 184 were refused by name.
  - In every plan, every feed sample and every rapid sample below the top was checked against the line's cutter-centre band (W/2 - r). The worst excess was **+0.000001 mm**, and no move went below the floor.
- **Degenerate inputs, all refused cleanly with no panic:** step 0, -1, NaN or inf; width NaN, 0, negative, below D, equal to D, or 1e7 (the stock grid refuses it); loop width larger than the room, 0 or negative; engagement 0 or 500; lift 0; stepdown 1e-9 (the pass cap refuses it); top below bottom; a == b; a NaN endpoint; fewer than two points.
- **Polyline chains (library only - the op passes only a two-point line).** I tried an L turning left and right and an R30 arc in both directions. Every plan returned stayed inside the band, and every other case was refused by name.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **PR body is out of date.** It still says "kind 39" and "now pin index 38". After the merge of main, the kind is 40, plasma profile is 39, and the trochoid is the last row. Worth correcting so the cut's changelog row and the decision record agree. `docs/decisions/220-trochoidal-slot.md` already says 40.
2. **A too-small step gets a confusing refusal** (`trochoid_slot.rs:205`, `trochoid_loops.rs:221`). When every rung of the ladder exceeds `MAX_LOOPS` (e.g. step 1e-12), `layout` returns `None` on every rung. The message then reads "no forward step holds the 90.0 deg engagement limit - the least, inf deg at (0.000, 0.000), was read at a 0.0000 mm step". It is still a refusal, but naming the cause ("the forward step gives more than 20000 loops - raise it") would tell the user what to change.
3. **The microlift height has no upper bound** (`trochoid_slot.rs:123`, `sane.rs`). A 100 mm lift is accepted and the return runs at feed far above the clearance plane (it measured fine and is not a gouge). Consider capping it at the stepdown or at the retract/clearance plane.
4. **The helix falls back to one turn silently** (`trochoid_slot.rs:341`). `helix_turns(..).unwrap_or(1.0)` gives a single turn when the turn count would pass `MAX_HELIX_TURNS` (1024), which drops the whole depth in one revolution. Reaching it takes an extreme ratio of stepdown to band (1024 x 2B), so it is practically out of reach, but the Prime Directive prefers a named refusal to a silent fallback.
5. **Curved chains, for slice 2.** With the default loop width (B = room), any curvature is refused: the arc ends on the outer side sit a hair beyond the band. Even a gentle R30 arc gives "turns too tightly". Narrower loop widths often hit the crossing law near the bore and at bends instead. That is the safe outcome, but polyline centre lines will need a margin or a curvature-aware layout before they are useful in the op. Also, `contained()` checks the wall leads only at their endpoints. That is exact on a straight line, but on a bend's inner side the chord can sag past the wall (the sag is about step²/8R). No case in my sweep breached, but when polylines reach the op, sampling the leads like the arcs would close the gap.
6. **`generate.rs:1617-1624` (minor style).** The `region_for_job(...)` call in the new arm has inconsistent indentation.
7. **`TrochoidDto::from_params`** recurses through `retype_params` for a non-trochoid kind. That is fine while `retype_params(_, 40)` always yields a trochoid; a direct seed call would avoid relying on that.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
